samples.summary: Cell-aware range traversal re-implemented in the copy path instead of reusing `model/range-slices.ts`, the module that exists specifically to be the single traversal of "which blocks does a DocRange cover"
samples.evidence: `getSelectedBlocks()` now adds its own `layout.blockParentMap.get(start.blockId)` → `resolveNestedTableLayout` → `cell.blocks` → per-block `sliceStart/sliceEnd` walk. `packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:1-17` states it is "The one traversal that decides which text a `DocRange` covers" and was introduced precisely so read and write would not "keep two copies of the dispatch in sync" (issue #715); `visitRangeSlices` (lines 145-226) already implements the identical cross-block-inside-one-cell case (lines 165-190) with the same offset trimming. `TextEditor` holds `this.doc` (line 197) and already imports from this module (`dirtyBlockIdsForRange`, line 23), so reuse was available. The two copies already disagree: `visitRangeSlices` deliberately resolves via `doc.blockParentMap` and gives up on blocks in nested tables, while the new copy path resolves via `layout` + `resolveNestedTableLayout` and covers nested-table cells — so styling and copying can now report different coverage for the same selection, and the third copy must be kept in sync by hand.

The new provider (editor.ts:2253-2266) repeats block lookup + `findImageAtOffset` + null-guards already implemented at editor.ts:3652-3663 (`getSelectedImage`), differing only in field naming (`image` vs `data`) and `findBlock` vs `getBlock`. Two near-identical readers of the same view state will drift (they already differ in throw behaviour); one could be expressed in terms of the other.

samples.summary: The #870 outcome is only reachable by keyboard — the context menu still gates Cut/Copy on a *text* selection, so right-clicking a click-selected image offers neither
samples.evidence: `hasSelection = !!editor.getActiveSelection()` (line 74) reflects the text `Selection` only; the whole point of #870 is that a click-selected image is view-local state invisible to it. `showCut`/`showCopy` (lines 176-181) therefore stay false with an image selected, so the menu path for copying an image is still missing while the keyboard path was fixed. `EditorAPI.getSelectedImage()` was available to widen the predicate.

samples.summary: The canonical image design doc's keyboard table and Editor API section are not updated for the new copy/cut-over-selected-image behaviour and the two new TextEditor hooks
samples.evidence: docs-image-editing.md documents image selection as a first-class selection kind with an explicit keyboard table (lines 148-153: arrows / Delete / Esc) and an Editor API listing. The change adds Cmd/Ctrl+C and Cmd/Ctrl+X semantics over a selected image plus `imageSelectionProvider` / `imageDeleteHandler` on `TextEditor`, and also makes Delete/Backspace a no-op in read-only, none of which is recorded there. Behaviour still works as specified, so the cost is documentation drift in the canonical subsystem doc rather than user-visible.

samples.summary: Two behaviour changes ride along that neither #872 nor #870 asks for: a new read-only guard on inline image deletion, and Copy in the read-only context menu
samples.evidence: `deleteSelectedImageInline` adds `if (readOnly || !selectedImage) return;` (editor.ts:2243) — the old Delete/Backspace path had no read-only guard, so this silently changes read-only behaviour; and `docs-context-menu.tsx:181` flips `showCopy` to `hasSelection` alone. Both are plausible fixes, but they are separate defects folded into a copy-integrity branch, which makes the change harder to revert independently. (The read-only image-delete fix has no corresponding assertion in the new test file.)

samples.summary: Platform (mod-key) detection inlined a fourth time instead of reusing the package's existing check
samples.evidence: `/Mac|iPhone|iPad|iPod/.test(navigator.platform)` is copied into `imageKeyHandler`; `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:874` computes exactly the same `isMac`/`mod` pair, and the frontend has a shared `components/text-formatting/platform.ts`. A tiny shared helper in the docs view layer would keep the copy-shortcut definition in one place — relevant because the whole finding this branch had to fix was the two sites disagreeing about key normalization.

samples.summary: `writeImageToClipboard` claims to produce "the same shape an in-document image copy produces" but hardcodes `DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE`
samples.evidence: `sliceBlockRange` clones the source block's own `style` (line 3784), whereas the image copy writes `{ ...DEFAULT_BLOCK_STYLE }`, so a centred/indented paragraph containing the image pastes back with default block style. Minor fidelity divergence from the documented shape; behaviour otherwise matches the plan.

finding.summary: Cell-aware range traversal re-implemented in the copy path instead of reusing `model/range-slices.ts`, the module that exists specifically to be the single traversal of "which blocks does a DocRange cover"
finding.evidence: `getSelectedBlocks()` now adds its own `layout.blockParentMap.get(start.blockId)` → `resolveNestedTableLayout` → `cell.blocks` → per-block `sliceStart/sliceEnd` walk. `packages/docs/src/model/range-slices.ts:1-17` states it is "The one traversal that decides which text a `DocRange` covers" and was introduced precisely so read and write would not "keep two copies of the dispatch in sync" (issue #715); `visitRangeSlices` (lines 145-226) already implements the identical cross-block-inside-one-cell case (lines 165-190) with the same offset trimming. `TextEditor` holds `this.doc` (line 197) and already imports from this module (`dirtyBlockIdsForRange`, line 23), so reuse was available. The two copies already disagree: `visitRangeSlices` deliberately resolves via `doc.blockParentMap` and gives up on blocks in nested tables, while the new copy path resolves via `layout` + `resolveNestedTableLayout` and covers nested-table cells — so styling and copying can now report different coverage for the same selection, and the third copy must be kept in sync by hand.

verdict.reason: The code exists as quoted (text-editor.ts:3733-3759 resolves via layout.blockParentMap + resolveNestedTableLayout and slices cell.blocks in sliceBlockRange, 3766-3813), but the claimed reuse target cannot serve this path, so this is not a duplicate answer to the same question. visitRangeSlices reports only non-empty (blockId, from, to) text spans — range-slices.ts:16 states "Empty slices are never reported", enforced at :187 and :224 — whereas the copy path must emit a cloned block even for an empty slice (text-editor.ts:3779-3785 substitutes [{text:'',style:{}}]); reusing it would silently drop empty paragraphs inside a multi-block cell selection and drop the final block whenever a drag ends at offset 0, defeating the acceptance criterion "A cell copy spanning several blocks in one cell keeps each block's type" (docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-copy-paste-integrity-todo.md:56). The visitor also carries no Block, while copy must clone type/headingLevel/listKind/marker/style and deep tableData (3780-3808), and visitRangeSlices deliberately expands a covered table into per-cell slices (range-slices.ts:211-219) where copy must clone the table block whole. The module's own header scopes its invariant to style read/write agreement (range-slices.ts:2-16), not clipboard extraction. Where reuse was genuinely available the change takes it: resolveNestedTableLayout is the shared helper already used at 4323-4329, layout.blockParentMap is the same map getCellInfo reads (3355-3364), and the clone/trim loop was factored into one sliceBlockRange shared by the body and cell paths. The only residue is that the cell lookup is inline rather than via getCellInfo() — a three-line unfactored lookup whose cost stays inside the codebase, which this lens grades minor, and minor never blocks.
